- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 74+), then corrects downward — model fails to capture the “peak then drop” pattern.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized: model holds high values too long after peaks, ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days for the first 10–15 days, then catches up or diverges again.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- High initial forecast values (e.g., >75) are often followed by a sharp correction, but model doesn’t adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to reset expectations after a major drop, leading to persistent overestimation in subsequent days.
- Forecast bias is often toward higher values, especially when recent history shows downward trend — model resists mean reversion.
